headline: Drupal says a second core flaw is exploited; sites may already be compromised
plain_summary: Drupal says a second flaw in its core software is being used in attacks, and sites that left the installer reachable after the first advisory may already be compromised. A VirtueMart flaw for Joomla is also reported as exploited. Belgian researchers say a hacker used an AI agent to take data on about 1.2 million residents, though the national cyber centre cannot confirm the figures. Site owners running Drupal, Joomla or Ivanti Connect Secure should update.

items.title: Drupal core flaw CVE-2026-136716 exploited in the wild
items.why: Drupal rates it highly critical and says sites exposed after the earlier SA-CORE-2026-017 may already be compromised.
items.action: Drupal advises updating to the fixed version for your release line and running update.php, securing the installer, and checking logs for unauthorized access, especially to the user 1 account.

items.title: VirtueMart for Joomla: file inclusion flaw exploited
items.why: The CVE record says the unauthenticated flaw in versions 4.0.0 through 4.8.7 has been exploited and could allow remote code execution.
items.action: Update the VirtueMart extension to 4.8.8, the version the CVE record says fixes the flaw.

items.title: Ivanti Connect Secure CVE-2026-104935 under scanning
items.why: F5 Labs recorded 46 exploitation attempts from 4 source IPs; the flaw has been in CISA KEV since October 13.
items.action: F5 Labs advises to patch now and apply Ivanti's fixed versions; per Ivanti's advisory data the flaw is fixed in ICS 25.1.3.0.

items.title: Hacker reportedly used DeepSeek agent on Flemish municipalities
items.why: Secutec and SOCRadar say data of about 1.2 million people in 82 municipalities was exposed; the CCB cannot confirm the figures and prosecutors are investigating.
items.action: Secutec and SOCRadar say multi-factor authentication and IP restrictions held off the attacks; SOCRadar published detection rules and indicators for IT teams to search their logs.

items.title: Binance: October 29 theft began with a malicious coding test
items.why: Binance executives say about $6.34 billion in assets were affected and an engineer was approached through a recruitment platform; the FBI is reported to attribute it to TraderTraitor.

items.title: Microsoft Office/Visio flaw CVE-2026-112732 patched
items.why: GovCERT.HK says a fix exists for Office LTSC 2021 and 2024; neither source says it is exploited.
items.action: GovCERT.HK advises affected users to apply the patches from Windows Update / Microsoft Update Catalog and follow the vendor's recommendations.

items.title: Hong Kong City Ticketing system hacked, about 1.3 million users
items.why: LCSD says names, phone numbers and emails may be involved; identity document details are not stored and card data is masked.

items.title: South Korea briefs firms on amended network act
items.why: Companies must designate a CISO as an executive, notify affected users of breaches, and can face fines for repeated breaches.
